The error
java.lang.InternalError: Can't start the AWT because Java was started  
on the first thread.  Make sure StartOnFirstThread is not specified in  
your application's Info.plist or on the command line
occurs because Mac OS X Leopard requires AWT to run in the first  
thread. A possible way to solve this is to run the AWT headless (you  
can give the option to run AWT headless to the JVM). Running awt  
headless solves this problem but if you need the AWT, you will  
probably get an java.awt.HeadlessException. The option "--enable-

messages.subject: Re: rJava on Leopard
messages.body_plain:
I the error below is fixed in the SVN (see http://www.rforge.net/ 
rJava/ ). You get one step further with threads (i.e. you'll be able  
to start AWT), but you have to be very careful in what you do or it  
will deadlock very quickly. Essentially you cannot use any callbacks,  
because they can potentially call the main loop (as a part of R's  
event loop) which will freeze. I know, it is a very bad design on  
Apple's side, but unfortunately we cannot do anything about it.  
Currently the only reliable solution is to use JGR (or go back to  
Tiger ;)).

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Freebsd Solution for rJava etc!
messages.body_plain:
Solved my own problem so passing on the solution so it may help others.

Did some more digging around my error messages with Google.

Turns out posix semaphores are not enabled by default in the FreeBSD kernel.

The solution is to load this kernel module as follows before starting an R 
session where you want to use rJava or JavaGD or JRG etc:

"kldload sem"

If you don't have it you may need to recompile the kernel with

options P1003_1B_SEMAPHORES  - as per sys/conf/NOTES

or manually

cd /usr/src/sys/modules/sem 
make obj && make depend && make && make install
kldload sem

It would be great if this could be added to the installation notes for rJava 
with respect to FreeBSD (possible the other BSDs too).

Would have saved me a lot of time!!

I don't think the above is widely known about BSD beyond the kernel  guys.

It always gives a helpful "bad system call" if you don't have the sem module 
loaded.

Regards
